html:
Point Peninsula was a Middle Woodland culture of the St. Lawrence and Ottawa valleys, southern Ontario and New York. On this map it covers about 100 BCE to 500 CE. It is named after a site on Point Peninsula in Jefferson County, New York, on the shore of Lake Ontario.

Point Peninsula people fished, hunted and gathered, and made pottery pressed with toothed stamps and rocking marks. Some of their burials hold goods and customs from the Hopewell exchange world to the south, such as copper, shell and stone pipes.

They lived beside the Laurel people to the northwest and the Saugeen people to the west. Many archaeologists see them as ancestors of the later Owasco people of New York, and through them of Iroquoian speakers such as the Iroquois and Huron, though this is debated.
